The Definition of Continuity

This scene shows what continuity means at a point. Move the point a, then lift one value and watch continuity break.

There is one condition. The height you approach must equal the height at the point. Changing a single value breaks that agreement. The graph then tears at that point.

For example, draw the graph with a ✏️ pencil without lifting it. If one stroke suffices, the function is continuous. If one point floats above the rest, you must lift the pencil there.

Prove that sums and products of continuous functions are continuous, and deduce that every polynomial is continuous.

  4. We show xnx^nxn is continuous by induction.

    Base cases: for n=0n = 0n=0, x0=1x^0 = 1x0=1 is the constant function proved continuous above; for n=1n = 1n=1, x1=xx^1 = xx1=x is the identity proved continuous above.

    Inductive step: if xnx^nxn is continuous, then xn+1=xn⋅xx^{n+1} = x^n \cdot xxn+1=xn⋅x is a product of continuous functions, hence continuous by the product rule.

    So xnx^nxn is continuous for every n≥0n \ge 0n≥0.

    Then cxnc x^ncxn is continuous (constant times continuous, by the product rule), and any polynomial — a finite sum of such terms ckxkc_k x^kck​xk — is continuous (the sum rule, applied finitely many times).

Prove ∣x∣\lvert x\rvert∣x∣ is continuous at 000 with δ=ε\delta = \varepsilonδ=ε.

∣∣x∣−0∣=∣x∣<ε\left\lvert \lvert x\rvert - 0 \right\rvert = \lvert x\rvert < \varepsilon∣∣x∣−0∣=∣x∣<ε
Show proof

  1. We need ∣x−0∣<δ⇒∣∣x∣−∣0∣∣<ε\lvert x - 0\rvert < \delta \Rightarrow \lvert \lvert x\rvert - \lvert 0\rvert \rvert < \varepsilon∣x−0∣<δ⇒∣∣x∣−∣0∣∣<ε. But ∣∣x∣−0∣=∣x∣\lvert \lvert x\rvert - 0\rvert = \lvert x\rvert∣∣x∣−0∣=∣x∣, so it suffices to get ∣x∣<ε\lvert x\rvert < \varepsilon∣x∣<ε.

  2. Put δ=ε\delta = \varepsilonδ=ε: then ∣x−0∣=∣x∣<δ=ε\lvert x - 0\rvert = \lvert x\rvert < \delta = \varepsilon∣x−0∣=∣x∣<δ=ε is exactly the desired inequality. Hence ∣x∣\lvert x\rvert∣x∣ is continuous at 000.

  3. [framing] Continuity does not imply differentiability: ∣x∣\lvert x\rvert∣x∣ is not differentiable at 000. Continuity is "no breaks", not "smoothness".
